answer.evidence: The tile is a full-width 48px opaque field, rows 0-31, of olive-peat checker texture with a few faint horizontal step lines (rows ~11, ~24) that suggest ramp steps. It has dark edges on the left and right sides (rows 7-31) as cut walls. The whole tile is a flat ground surface seen from above. No front face of 3+ rows is drawn, only a slightly lighter strip at the bottom (rows 30-31). For terrain, this reads as a top-down ramp surface rather than a standing object.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate reads as a tan/olive block split into three horizontal bands with thin darker separator lines. Each band is a smooth gradient or fill with almost no grain, speckle, clumps or per-pixel texture, so it looks like a striped sticker beside the references. The grass reference has tufts and clumps, and the paving reference has stones shaded one by one. The measured facts are not bad: 7 visible tones per tile (grass 3, paving 7) and 4% near-flat coverage. But the candidate has only 11 distinct colours in total, against 80 for the grass, and the picture shows about 4 real lightness steps against the 5-6 of Beodeul. About 49% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, which is a mix of tinted and neutral lines. The peat-cliff ramp has no soil grain, no root or strata detail and no per-band highlights. It is not rich enough to sit next to the references, so I fail it.
